Beware: Check the NSF ratings - This product is supposedly certified to the NSF 42 & 372 standards. However, NSF 42 means it "reduces aesthetic impurities such as chlorine and taste/odor ". And NSF 372 means the product does not leach lead into the water (i.e. it says nothing about whether or not it removes lead from the water).

The important NSF standards for water filtration are NSF 42, 53, 401. NSF 53 is designed to "reduce specific health-related contaminants." NSF 401 is designed to "remove up to 15 individual contaminants which
have been identified in published studies as occurring in drinking water."

So if you only care about NSF 42 (taste) and care less about actual health-related contaminants, these filters seem fine. If you care about health-related contaminants, I'd look elsewhere.

Pros
- cheap
- small
- spins clothes to nearly dry

Cons
- makes more noise than a standard washer
- can only wash a small amount at a time
- more time consuming than a standard washer if you are doing more than one load

Tips
- do your laundry daily (or if you rewear clothes then do it when you have 2 outfits to wash)

- sit it in the tub and fill it with the shower head if you have a removable shower head. It makes it so much easier than trying to get it to attach to a faucet.

- do NOT over load it, it won't break but it won't properly agitate the clothes either.

- keep in mind that a standard washer drains and fills almost as much as this thing, you just don't see it because it does it automatically.

Replaced Whirlpool (wdt710paym6) Dishwasher element , but adjustments were needed. Includes nuts! - Listed as replacement part for W10518394 (Whirlpool part number for my dishwasher). I ultimately got it to work with my dishwasher, however, there are a few issues. It was the right shape and the element was the right size. The spade connectors were also the right fit for the electrical connections. But, 1. The threads do not match the original plastic nuts, so you cant use the original / more convenient nuts. I expected this, based reviews of many other elements being sold as replacements. Which is why I chose this particular one on Amazon because this seller was one of very few sellers that listed the item with included nuts. (Much appreciated! added the fourth star.) The ones that were included with this item worked fine, but a deep well socket is required / recommended to install them. I would also recommend installing them with a washer so that the edges of the nuts are not digging into the plastic dishwasher basin. 2. A little more of an issue, the threaded parts of the element were too wide to fit through the holes of the dishwasher basin. I may have been able to force it through but it would have required a significant amount of force and I did not want to risk damaging the dishwasher or the part. Instead, I used a Dremel to slightly widen the holes in the dishwasher basin (Very carefully, as I had to make sure the hole was small enough and uniform for the sealing washer to still seal). After making the above modifications, I was able to install the element. It is working well so far. No leaks. My dishwasher is drying once again and washing better as the water is actually hot throughout the cycle. I can recommend this item, just be prepared for some possible modifications.

Correct Part Number, Wrong Rod Measurements - The part number sent was correct for the refrigerator model; however, the rod would need to be ground down in order for the original washers/spacers to fit on properly as others have noted. I don't have a grinder and my attempts to modify with a wetstone were not successful. I returned this part and ordered another auger, OEM, and paid twice as much but still had a similar issue. Watched YouTube videos; checked schematics. My original auger had 2 metal washers plus a plastic spacer on the rod just before the plastic spirals started. Schematics and videos showed 1 spacer or sometimes 2 spacers. One YouTube video showed that the measurements were different between end of rod and the notch in the rod right before the plastic started. Apparently there was a change in mfg specs at some point in time. My refrig is 11 years old. I couldn't make this part work and so returned it but managed to get the OEM auger to function by removing the 2 metal washers after seeing the YouTube video and checking the measurements. I can now get ice cubes plus crushed ice. Taking it apart and putting back together was not difficult but getting it to work properly was. May work fine for newer refrigerators.
